description: Whether the invocation-precondition step requires a caller-supplied commit identity, whose absence refuses the run with `identity_invalid` before the policy runs.
given: an entry point and the policy the invocation would run
expect: whether a commit identity is required as a precondition
notes: The answer is a property of the entry point alone (Section 8.6): a front-end sequence that dispatches one means the sequence's own dispatches (Sections 12.2, 12.3), so a policy's `run_op` edges do not widen the set. `policy` is supplied in every vector so that independence is asserted rather than assumed.

A `false` answer does not mean the invocation writes no commit. An entry outside the set MAY reach `commit`, `integrate` or `pull` through a `run_op` edge, because a policy is a graph (Section 5.2); with no identity supplied that operation reports `identity_missing`, class `needs_caller`, at the dispatch (Section 4.3). That is behavior against a real backend and is not exercised here; the reason token is in `vocabulary.json` under `reasons`.

Whether a supplied identity is well formed is judged by the backend through `accepts_identity` (Sections 8.6, 9.1), whatever the entry, and is deferred with the rest of plugin behavior. This function answers only whether one is required.

vectors.description: An entry that can write a commit (Section 8.6).
A merge commit `integrate` writes carries the same identity (Section 10.1).
The sequence dispatches `commit` and `integrate` of its own (Section 12.2).
The sequence dispatches `merge` alone, which the forge performs and the engine supplies no identity for (Sections 12.3, 10.1).
A policy edge dispatching `commit` from a read-only entry's outcome leaves the precondition unchanged; the dispatch reports `commit:identity_missing` instead (Sections 4.3, 8.6).
The routing Section 6.5 illustrates and Section 12.2 builds in, invoked at the `push` entry point.
